outcomes.question: What are the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
outcomes.answer: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: Why does the framework advise to stop guessing capacity needs?
outcomes.answer:
Making a poor capacity decision when deploying a workload can result in paying for expensive idle resources or suffering from the performance impacts of limited capacity. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Cloud computing allows organizations to use only the required capacity and scale in and out automatically. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 11]
Resource saturation, occurring when workload demands exceed capacity, is a common reason for failure in on-premises systems. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 13]

outcomes.question: What is the difference between one-way door and two-way door decisions?
outcomes.answer:
Two-way doors are reversible decisions that can utilize a lightweight process. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
One-way doors are difficult or impossible to reverse and require greater inspection prior to being made. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 69]
Organizations are advised to centralize one-way door decisions that may be irreversible. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]
Two-way door decisions can be permitted to be made by lower-level organizational leaders. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 26]

outcomes.question: What is the AWS Well-Architected Tool?
outcomes.answer:
The AWS Well-Architected Tool is a cloud service that offers a consistent process to review and measure your architecture using the AWS Well-Architected Framework. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
The tool is provided by AWS to review workloads at no charge. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
It provides recommendations designed to make workloads more reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 7]
AWS provides the tool to review your approach before development, workload states before production, and workloads in production. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]
Using the tool, you can compare workloads against the latest AWS architectural best practices, monitor status, and gain insight into potential risks. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 12]

outcomes.question: What does recovery time objective (RTO) mean?
outcomes.answer:
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) represents the maximum acceptable delay between a service interruption and the restoration of that service. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
RTO establishes an acceptable time window during which the service is unavailable, as defined by the organization. [disaster-recovery-workloads-on-aws.pdf, p. 13]
RTO serves as a target or maximum allowed value for a single availability-impacting event. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 19]

outcomes.question: How should a client retry failed requests without overloading a service?
outcomes.answer:
Exponential backoff should be used to retry requests after progressively longer intervals. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Jitter should be introduced to randomize retry intervals and avoid request alignment into spikes. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Adding exponential backoff with jitter allows servers to recover when failures stem from resource overload. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Configuring a maximum number of retries or elapsed time is important to prevent creating backlogs that lead to metastable failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]
Retries should be implemented at only one layer of the application stack to avoid compounding attempts into a retry storm. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 545]

outcomes.question: Why should a workload be aware of service quotas and constraints?
outcomes.answer:
Being aware of and managing service quotas and resource constraints helps customers prevent service degradation or disruption in their AWS accounts. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
Monitoring and automatically managing service quotas and resource constraints can proactively reduce failures. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 470]
If a constraint is reached unexpectedly, an account's applications or services can suffer degradation or disruption. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 24]

outcomes.question: How does the reliability pillar suggest recovering automatically from failures?
outcomes.answer:
Automation can be triggered when a threshold is breached by monitoring a workload for key performance indicators (KPIs). [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Workload KPIs should focus on measuring business value rather than the technical aspects of service operation. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Monitoring KPIs enables automatic notification and tracking of failures, as well as automated recovery processes to work around or repair them. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]
Failures can be anticipated and remediated before they occur when using more sophisticated automation. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 38]

outcomes.question: Who is responsible for what in the shared responsibility model for security?
outcomes.answer:
Security and Compliance is a shared responsibility between AWS and the customer. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS is responsible for 'Security of the Cloud', which entails protecting the infrastructure that runs all of the services offered in the AWS Cloud, composed of hardware, software, networking, and facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
AWS operates, manages, and controls components from the host operating system and virtualization layer down to the physical security of the facilities. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
The customer is responsible for 'Security in the Cloud', determined by the specific AWS Cloud services the customer selects. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
The customer assumes responsibility for managing the guest operating system (including updates and security patches), other associated application software, and configuring the AWS provided security group firewall. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Under the model, AWS secures the underlying cloud infrastructure, while the customer is responsible for securing applications, data, and the services used. [wellarchitected-security-pillar.pdf, p. 130]

outcomes.question: What is the principle of least privilege?
outcomes.answer:
The principle of least privilege states that identities should only be allowed to perform the minimum set of actions required to carry out a specific task. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
This principle strikes a balance between usability, efficiency, and security. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]
Following this principle assists in restricting unintended access and tracking who can access specific resources. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 319]

outcomes.question: How does the operational excellence pillar recommend making changes to workloads?
outcomes.answer:
The operational excellence pillar recommends making frequent, small, reversible changes by designing workloads that are scalable and loosely coupled so components can be updated regularly. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Combining smaller, incremental changes with automated deployment techniques reduces the blast radius and allows for faster reversal if failures occur. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Emphasizing frequent, small, reversible changes limits the scope of change, resulting in faster troubleshooting, remediation, and the ability to roll back changes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 82]

outcomes.question: What are runbooks used for?
outcomes.answer:
Runbooks are documented processes consisting of a series of steps used to achieve a specific outcome. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
In cloud operations, runbooks are utilized to lower risk and accomplish desired outcomes. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks provide codified processes for activities ranging from onboarding new personnel to releasing major deployments. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 141]
Runbooks are frequently used for routine activities rather than non-routine events. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]
Even in workloads that are highly automated, runbooks serve to run game days and satisfy reporting and auditing standards. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 592]

outcomes.question: How can feature flags and A/B testing be used to experiment safely?
outcomes.answer:
Feature flags and A/B testing can be used to safely conduct experiments and collect feedback from users. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
AWS AppConfig Feature Flags offers functionality to create feature flags. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
A/B testing allows organizations to validate new features using feedback from real users. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
AWS Lambda versions can be utilized to deploy a function's new version for beta testing. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 128]
Feature-flag testing allows an individual feature to be flagged on and off from outside the application so each new feature can be validated one at a time. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]
A/B testing provides comparative results between two user testing groups against the current version. [wellarchitected-operational-excellence-pillar.pdf, p. 133]

outcomes.question: What does democratize advanced technologies mean in the performance efficiency pillar?
outcomes.answer:
Democratizing advanced technologies means making advanced technology implementation easier by delegating complex tasks to your cloud vendor. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Instead of having an IT team learn to host and run a new technology, organizations can consume that technology as a service. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Technologies requiring specialized expertise, like NoSQL databases, media transcoding, and machine learning, become cloud services teams can consume. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]
Consuming these technologies as services allows teams to focus on product development instead of resource provisioning and management. [wellarchitected-performance-efficiency-pillar.pdf, p. 9]

outcomes.question: How should failed Lambda transactions be retained and retried?
outcomes.answer:
A dead-letter queue mechanism should be used to retain, investigate, and retry failed transactions. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Failed transactions can be sent to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue dedicated on a per function basis in AWS Lambda. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Lambda allows configuration of Maximum Retry Attempts, Maximum Record Age, and Destination on Failure to control retries when processing data records. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]
Poison-pill messages can be removed from a batch by sending their metadata to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue for further analysis. [wellarchitected-serverless-applications-lens.pdf, p. 60]

outcomes.question: What options does AWS offer for service discovery of microservices?
outcomes.answer:
Amazon ECS offers integrated DNS-based service discovery using the Route 53 Auto Naming API to create and manage a registry of service names. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Unified service discovery is available for Kubernetes-managed services through AWS contributions to the External DNS project. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS Cloud Map provides service discovery via an API-based mechanism and acts as a service registry for resources like IPs, URLs, and ARNs. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Third-party distributed key-value stores such as HashiCorp Consul, etcd, or Netflix Eureka can be used to implement service discovery, including via an AWS Quick Start for HashiCorp Consul. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
Service meshes provide an additional layer to handle interservice communication, enabling tasks like service discovery to be managed completely by that layer. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 17]
AWS App Mesh can be utilized in service-oriented architectures to provide reliable discovery and access of services. [wellarchitected-reliability-pillar.pdf, p. 65]

outcomes.question: What do twelve-factor processes say about state?
outcomes.answer:
The Processes section states that twelve-factor processes are stateless and share-nothing. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]
Any data needing persistence must be saved in a stateful backing service, typically a database. [microservices-on-aws.pdf, p. 14]

outcomes.question: What does it mean to adopt a consumption model?
outcomes.answer:
Adopting a consumption model means paying only for the computing resources that you consume. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]
It also involves increasing or decreasing your resource usage based on business requirements. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]
Resources can be stopped when not in use, such as development and test environments that are typically only used for eight hours a day during the work week, yielding a potential cost savings of 75%. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 8]

You can stop these resources when they’re not in use for a potential cost savings of 75% (40 hours versus 168 hours)."}]}

outcomes.question: How does the cost optimization pillar suggest reducing cloud waste?
outcomes.answer:
Organizations should identify and recoup expenditure tied to cloud waste for resources that are deployed. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Cloud waste happens when resources are created with incorrect sizing or when unexpected usage patterns are observed. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
To reduce waste, organizations can follow AWS best practices or seek assistance from their account team and partner to optimize cloud costs. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Periodically generating reports of Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, and Amazon EC2 rightsizing recommendations from AWS Cost Explorer helps reduce costs related to idle, underutilized, and steady-state resources. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 28]
Attributing resource costs to workloads, individual organizations, or product owners promotes efficient usage behavior and aids in reducing waste. [wellarchitected-cost-optimization-pillar.pdf, p. 37]

outcomes.question: Why does the choice of AWS Region matter for the carbon footprint of a workload?
outcomes.answer:
The selection of an AWS Region has a significant impact on workload KPIs, specifically performance, cost, and carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 935]
Placing a workload in Regions with low published carbon intensity or near Amazon renewable energy projects helps reduce its carbon footprint. [wellarchitected-framework.pdf, p. 935]

outcomes.question: What is the shared responsibility model for sustainability?
outcomes.answer:
Environmental sustainability is defined as a shared responsibility between customers and AWS. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
AWS carries responsibility for sustainability of the cloud, which includes delivering efficient, shared infrastructure, water stewardship, and sourcing renewable power. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
Customers carry responsibility for sustainability in the cloud by optimizing workloads, resource utilization, and minimizing total resources required to deploy workloads. [wellarchitected-sustainability-pillar.pdf, p. 7]
